text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday.
- Croatian government allots three million kuna in aid to flooded areas.
- Experts of the Hague war crimes tribunal unearth the first body from a mass grave estimated to contain 170-260 Croats from Vukovar allegedly executed by Yugoslav Army in 1991.
- Prime minister Zlatko Matesa says Croatia has a solid partner in EBRD, which has so far invested some $300 million in various projects.
- World Bank finances the purchase of goats for Croatian breeders as part of its $19.7 million emergency loan for agriculture.
- Government proposes a strategy for the road network construction, estimated to require up to $8 billion.
- Interest rate on loans to farmers for the financing of autumn sowings cut down to 8.5 from 12 percent.
- Railway company Hrvatske Zeljeznice, Siemens sign agreement for the purchase and refurbishment of carriages.
- OSCE funds Bosnian election campaign of Serbian paramilitary leader Zeljko Raznjatovic Arkan.
- Succession talks continue in Brussels: Representative of rump Yugoslavia lays claims to most of pre-1991 assets. Others insists on equal division among successor states.
- Reconstruction of war-damaged houses in Sibenik hinterland hampered by masses of red tape. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
